title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1971-04-29
lineage: AKG190E > Uher 400L > Technics 1506 > Cardas audiophile cables > HHB CDR 800 master CD > CD > Plextor PX-708A > EAC v0.95pb5 > CD Wave > shntool v1.01 > FLAC16

ai_review.summary: A classic 1971 show with smoking Alligator>Cold Rain, Hard to Handle and Midnight Hour, but the audience‑tape recording is muddy, full of silences and far from clean.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about this performance – the Alligator → Cold Rain sequence, a fiery Hard to Handle, and Bill’s thunderous drumming on Minglewood are repeatedly called out as highlights.  The recording, however, is an audience tape plagued by long gaps, low‑level mix and missing sections, making it a painful listen despite the show’s high energy.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is rated very high by most reviewers (top‑10 status, multiple 5‑star praises) while the recording quality is consistently described as poor; weighted average yields ~4.0 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audience tape with long silences, low‑level mix and occasional drop‑outs; many reviewers note missing energy and recommend seeking a soundboard version.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong mid‑set jams and classic numbers, though some reviewers note missing tracks (Cumberland → Playing) and a reversed Loser/Dark Hollow order in the digital copy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals described as uninspired at times; his solo is mentioned but compared unfavorably to other dates.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass praised as strong, distinct and ‘bombs’ on Sugar Magnolia; highlighted throughout the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pig‑Pen rap on Hard to Handle noted; no snide remarks or banter captured in this tape.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill's drumming on Minglewood is singled out as a highlight; overall drum work praised.
